headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: AutoGen’s broad file/network execution can expose course secrets and amplify unverified outputs in the paired RAG workflow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write the filesystem and execute shell commands, while the course agent also reads/writes files and exposes API endpoints. A shared workspace or copied outputs could let content from one agent be treated as instructions by the other. No direct shared-channel evidence is provided, so this is inferred and kept at medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same working directory, injected file content can cross from one agent to the other.
IF either agent parses the other’s file output as instructions, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Use separate working directories for each agent.
Add a manual review step before one agent consumes the other’s files.
Prefix inter-agent files with provenance metadata.
Disable automatic ingestion of generated documents.
requires-engineering: add content provenance checks in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch files and secrets: AutoGen handles model provider API keys, and the course agent handles configuration secrets plus API tokens. With broad filesystem access and local development deployment, a shared workspace can leak sensitive data between them. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default-style setups, so severity is high.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or mounted workspace, secrets written by one can be read by the other.
IF either agent logs or echoes file contents into outputs, those secrets can be exposed further.
mitigations: Review logs for accidental secret emission.
requires-engineering: enforce secret redaction at the orchestrator boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have shell execution, subprocess spawning, package installation, and filesystem write access. Even though neither profile claims git writes, overlapping mutable access to the same directory can still cause race conditions and overwrite conflicts. The interaction is documented by capabilities, but not enough for high because git-state conflict is not present.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory concurrently, file overwrites can occur.
IF one agent installs packages while the other runs code from the same environment, environment drift can break tasks.
mitigations: requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen is a multi-agent orchestration framework that can emit tool-driven outputs, and the course agent is a content-writing/RAG system with ask/stream endpoints. If the course agent consumes AutoGen output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into generated papers, answers, or downstream actions. The pathway is plausible in default workflows and can affect multiple work products.
conditions: IF the course agent uses AutoGen-generated text as source material without verification, hallucinations can propagate.
IF either agent auto-renders or auto-answers from the other’s output, downstream mistakes multiply.
mitigations: Add a human approval step for generated claims.
Disable automatic action-taking from model text.
requires-engineering: implement verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: The course agent explicitly handles academic papers, paper metadata, research questions, and configuration secrets, while AutoGen handles application data and model-provider keys. If regulated or sensitive data is placed into the course workflow, the local-development and broad-network setup can create retention or residency mismatches. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction breach, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF EU personal data or PHI is entered into the course workflow, residency/compliance obligations may apply.
IF logs retain secrets or paper data longer than policy allows, retention compliance is violated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
